previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of mitochondrial myopathy, coronary artery disease, and orthostatic intolerance was admitted for worsening lightheadedness, chest pressure, nausea, and dehydration over five days. He presented proactively due to concern for renal complications from poor oral intake. In the emergency department, he received IV fluids with symptom improvement. Evaluation showed no acute cardiac injury, with normal troponins and unchanged EKG. Chest imaging revealed no acute pathology. He was treated with over four liters of IV normal saline, which corrected orthostasis and improved renal function. His symptoms, including chest pain, abdominal discomfort, and pleuritic pain, resolved with rehydration. He was discharged home in stable condition with a new prescription for ondansetron for breakthrough nausea and instructions to maintain hydration and follow up with cardiology and neurology.

___ yo M w/ CAD (see below, multiple PCIs), HTN, HL, Afib not on

# CORONARIES:  Presenting with chest pressure similar to 
previous MI, concerning for UA vs. NSTEMI vs. demand angina ___ 
dehydration vs. arrhythmia vs. PE. EKG in ED reported as having 
showed ST depressions in V4-V6, apparently new (though unable to 
locate that ECG as did not come up in chart). Repeat EKG while 
patient was CP free was not checked in the ED. NSTEMI less 
likely given that first troponins negative. Repeat EKG on floors 
while chest pain free showed no ST depression in leads V4-V6, 
and was sinus. He has had multiple admissions for nausea, chest 
pressure with dehydration. Orthostatic on admission with BP drop 
of 60 pts systolic, making dehydration and demand angina more 
likely. PE thought to be unlikely given no tachycardia, no 
pleuritic CP, no hypoxia, and no evidence on EKG. Arrhythmia 
associated with CP also possible, but in sinus bradycardia to 
high 50's, without events on telemetry. Troponins were negative 
x3. His repeat EKG was sinus bradycardia, unchanged. He was 
continued on home dose of ASA 325mg daily, Plavix 75mg daily. 
Lipids checked with LDL 61, TSH was 1.3, and A1c of 5.8. He was 
given aggressive fluid of 5L and symptoms completely resolved. 
He was continued on valsartan 80 bid, metoprolol succ 25 mg bid. 
Continued on antianginal Ranexa 500mg po bid (pt stated that 
Imdur previously has cause hypotension).
On the day of discharge, his chest pressure had completely 
resolved. He was instructed to ___ with his cardiologist, 
Dr. ___ as an outpatient.
He was also encouraged to increase his po intake and liberalize 
his salt diet given orthostasis. He was encouraged to use 
compression stockings as well.

Metoprolol succinate 25mg bid and Valsartan 80mg bid.

plavix. CHADS score 1 for HTN. Has been considered by ___ in 
___ for Reveal device. No events on telemetry, and remained 
in sinus. Continued on metoprolol succ as above, ASA 325mg daily 
and Plavix.

this admission. He has been seen by neurology previously in the 
autonomics department. We spoke with his autonomics physicians, 
who were very helpful stating that he will always be orthostatic 
given his dysautonomia. On the day of discharge, he was 
orthostatic, but asymptomatic without lightheadedness and 
ambulating well. As above, advised to increase his po intake and 
liberalize his salt diet given orthostasis. He was encouraged to 
use compression stockings as well. 
He was scheduled to ___ with autonomics as an outpatient.
